newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey, U.S. say wheat trade row practically over.
newsitem.headline: Turkey, U.S. say wheat trade row practically over.

text.p: Turkish and U.S. officials said on Wednesday a dispute between the two countries over Turkey's crackdown on imported wheat from the United States had practically ended.
"Both sides have agreed to end the issue. It is now practically over," a Turkish agriculture official told Reuters.
"Either a protocol will be signed or the principle agreement will be documented through an exchange of letter," he said.
"The dispute is now over. We are now discussing other issues with Turkey," said a U.S. official in Ankara.
He did not elaborate on the content of the discussions.

The U.S. stopped issuing phytosanitary certificates to grains exports to Turkey in October, after Ankara held up several cargoes of U.S. wheat to inspect for ergot fungus under zero-tolerance quarantine laws.

Zero-tolerance was seen as too stringent by U.S. officials and local millers, and Turkey raised the tolerance to 0.05 percent -- which is the internationally accepted level -- after local wheat prices had shot up by 30 percent.
Turkish and U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) officials have been discussing the issue since Monday.
Turkish officials said earlier in the week Turkey would not seek health clearances for five other types of grain diseases.
The Turkish official said there was now no U.S. wheat being held up at any Turkish port.
U.S. officials said more than 100,000 tonnes of milling wheat were en route to Turkey.
The USDA delegation is expected to leave Ankara later today.
